slot.brief: Find the range of a rational function f(x) = (linear)/(quadratic) by setting y = f(x) and demanding real x (discriminant ≥ 0).

solution:
Let $y=\dfrac{3x}{x^2+4}$. For real $x$, the quadratic $yx^2-3x+4y=0$ must have discriminant non-negative:
$$9-16y^2\ge 0\quad\Rightarrow\quad -\dfrac{3}{4}\le y\le\dfrac{3}{4}.$$
Equality is attained at $x=\pm2$, so the range is $\left[-\dfrac{3}{4},\dfrac{3}{4}\right]$.
